Forensics: v0<->v1 wall traced to local-alloc.c:472 reg_n_deaths==1 gate; reused load-temp (3 deaths) punted to global, single-death mask grabs v0 locally first. Flip needs a fresh single-death local

frontier.hypothesis: A cheat-free C shape could give the reused load-web reg_n_deaths==1 (making it LOCAL and higher-priority than the mask so it grabs v0) while preserving target's interleaved lw/sw scheduling.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c:472 punts the load-web to global only because reuse creates 3 deaths. If the web were single-death it would be local and win v0 over the mask (target layout). But reuse is what creates the WAR anti-deps that preserve the interleave; separate single-use temps (single-death, local) let sched1 hoist the loads together (s2: score 11), breaking the interleave. The tension (reuse-for-schedule vs single-death-for-RA) is the crux.
frontier.next_probe: Search for a forward-order C structure that yields single-death load pseudos (local) that local-alloc COALESCES into one v0 qty via combine_regs (move coalescing) WITHOUT sched1 hoisting the loads -- e.g. an anti-dependence source other than temp-reuse (a store-to-load ordering fence expressible in pure C) that serializes the loads while keeping each load pseudo single-death. Verify via .lreg reg_n_deaths + .sched insn order.

frontier.hypothesis: A cheat-free C shape could make the interleaved MASK a multi-death pseudo so it too is punted to global, where the higher-ref load-web (n_refs 6) outranks it and takes v0, leaving the mask v1 (target).
frontier.mechanism: If the mask had reg_n_deaths>=2 it fails the local-alloc.c:472 gate and both pseudos go to global.c, ordered by allocno priority (n_refs*freq/length): the 6-ref load-web beats the 2-ref mask for v0. The mask is single-death today because lui/ori is an in-place RMW (flow counts 1 death at the final sw).
frontier.next_probe: Find a pure-C mask construction whose value genuinely dies and is reborn (2 deaths) without a dead store and without adding an insn -- combine currently re-merges split constants (s3, score 9). Check whether any pure-C expression of 0xFFFFEF produces two REG_DEAD notes in the .flow dump while still assembling to lui/ori.
